body:
I took a quick look at the commit in question (https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/9709/commits/b4d894c06709b4ae807d540dfda21ab3220a989a) and the libuv docs (http://docs.libuv.org/en/v1.x/fs.html#c.uv_fs_copyfile), and I think the problem is that we're copying the literal file that we're editing, i.e. the symlink, instead of the file that our link is pointing to. Without the flag that the commit added, libuv appears to have been following through the symlink to get to the underlying file, while with the flag it doesn't follow the link.

If that's truly the case, then that seems like an inconsistency on libuv's part and the real change needs to be made upstream there.

> Alternatively, we omit UV_FS_COPYFILE_FICLONE if the file looks like a symlink.

If we're already talking about identifying symlinks, then we might as well finish the job by calling `readlink` on it and passing the underlying file to the copy function. Observed behavior is the same, but maybe we can keep the perf. benefits of supporting CoW.

I'll see if I can whip up a PR quickly and get your thoughts on it.
I'm new to the GitHub workflow, but I think I've figured how to push a PR. Now to figure out how to link it to the ticket... https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/10102

> is it expected that UV_FS_COPYFILE_FICLONE has this behavior for symlinks?

What version of libuv is neovim using? I ask because it appears that this issue is about macOS. In versions of prior to 1.28.0, libuv called mac's [`copyfile(3)`](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/copyfile.3.html). However, we received bug reports that `copyfile(3)` was not respecting file permissions. Starting with 1.28.0, macOS uses the same implementation as all other unix platforms. Here is the [commit](https://github.com/libuv/libuv/commit/5bc4d7738a172f6361d8b5dd0949789dcf1ff60d) where the macOS-specific implementation was removed, and [this](https://github.com/libuv/libuv/blob/4a4c9a688fa2a7fad056f48304a583927044b935/src/unix/fs.c#L902-L1029) is the current implementation.
I just ran a clean build and neovim pulled in libuv 1.26.0. It sounds like that's the source of the problem then.

- `vim -u DEFAULTS` (version: 8.0) behaves differently? Yes. It writes the backup to `/var/tmp` for a symlinked file
- Operating system/version: OS X 10.14.6
- Terminal name/version: iTerm2 3.3.6
- `$TERM`: `xterm-256color`

--------------------------------

Relates (I think) to #10101 (since it's about backups for symlinks).

Having `backupdir` set to a list of dirs where (in order of appearance) the first one does not exist, writing backups for symlink files will fail with `E506`.

When setting the `backupdir` option, the help indicates that it will attempt to create the backup file in the
> first directory in the list where this is possible

If one has this vimrc (only setting the backupdir):

```
set backupdir=~/.this-does-not-exist-tmp/,/var/tmp/
```

and the following files:

```
drwxr-xr-x  4 wspurgin  staff   128B Nov  7 10:17 .
drwxr-xr-x  7 wspurgin  staff   224B Nov  7 10:14 ..
lrwxr-xr-x  1 wspurgin  staff     7B Nov  7 10:14 bar.txt -> foo.txt
-rw-r--r--  1 wspurgin  staff    12B Nov  7 10:17 foo.txt
```

Attempt to edit `bar.txt` and then `:w` the file after it is open

### Actual behaviour

A `E506 Can't write backup file` error occurs when attempting to write `bar.txt`. Note, that if you swap the order of the directory list in `backupdir` (where a directory that exists appears first), there's no `E506`.

### Expected behaviour

I expect it to write the backup file to `/var/tmp` and not `E506`.
